A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EATcubic comparison study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-H support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling, gradient-quality, natural-image P-VAE, and synthetic POGLM experiments in Section 3 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and reports additional ImageNet, retinal-recording, Negative Binomial, macaque V1 readout, and limited-data results.

M1.justification: The proposed EATcubic procedure remains unchanged. The Gamma-Poisson adaptation already appeared in v1 Appendix H.3 and Algorithm 3. Corrections to GSM aggregation in Appendix C align it with v1's existing main-text formula; they do not establish a changed implemented method.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's van Hateren image patches and synthetic neural data, v2 evaluates ImageNet patches, recorded retinal ganglion-cell activity, and macaque V1 response prediction. The latter introduces a downstream neural-prediction task using pretrained features.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same comparators: EATsigmoid, GSM, score-function estimation, and exact gradients where available. Added experiments reuse these methods or subsets of them. Newly cited alternative VAEs are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing Appendix G protocols are retained, but added experiments introduce substantial settings: 40x40 inputs; RGC segmentation, a two-thirds training split, 30 epochs and 1-3 hidden neurons; fitted Negative Binomial dispersion with temperatures from 10^-6 to 0.5; frozen-feature linear readouts measured by explainable variance; and a 10,000-image training subset.

E4.justification: v2 adds limited-data overfitting analysis, Negative Binomial temperature sensitivity including extreme-temperature instability, and RGC robustness across hidden-neuron counts. These test additional failure conditions and applicability boundaries. The earlier firing-rate sweeps, Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses, and decoder visualizations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Existing results retain 100-trial standard errors, 100-sample gradient uncertainty, and three-seed training standard deviations. No changed replication counts or statistical estimation procedures are documented. The added readout results include uncertainty values but do not establish a different reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds RGC curves and Appendix H.3.1-H.3.4 outcomes. ImageNet ELBOs are -718.92 for exact gradients, -720.27 for EATcubic, and -755.40 for EATsigmoid. Macaque readout explainable variance is approximately 0.19, 0.22 +/- 0.01, and 0.24 +/- 0.01, respectively. These are newly reported experiments; original matched results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C corrects Gumbel-noise indexing, restores category-weighted aggregation in Eq. (24) and Algorithm 2, and clarifies the zero-temperature limit. Appendix E corrects the Poisson exponential sign in Eq. (56). The moment proofs, gradient/Hessian derivations, and dispersion formulations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims that EATcubic's favorable performance extends empirically to Negative Binomial latents and foregrounds GSM's broader applicability. The central contributions—systematic comparison, the cubic correction, and practical temperature-robustness guidance—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the persistent ImageNet gap as structural and proposes implicit regularization to explain improved neural readout and limited-data behavior. It also qualifies that temperature robustness does not necessarily transfer to readout accuracy and identifies extreme-temperature instability for Negative Binomial models. These substantially expand the earlier interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 supplies RGC processing/training instructions and basic setup details for the new appendix experiments, including previously unstated approximate original training/test counts. Conversely, Figure 12 omits the selected-temperature values shown in v1 Figure 15's legend. Code, data, and checkpoint access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning around metabolic costs and information geometry, references hybrid inference VAEs, and adds sources for neural datasets and explainable variance. The central novelty claim remains unchanged. Publication updates for Gumbel-Softmax/Concrete and the corrected wake-sleep bibliographic record refer to existing cited works.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory/background passages, expands the results roadmap, moves the dispersion discussion from H.3 to H.2, and organizes supplementary experiments into H.3.1-H.3.8. Author roles, affiliations, and acknowledgements are updated. Most core exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds RGC Figures 5 and 13, rearranges supplementary figure groups, and refines legends and page layout. For example, v1 Figures 13-15 become v2 Figures 10-12, with selected-temperature annotations removed from the last plot. Existing tables and most plot designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v1's practical recommendations relied on small image patches and synthetic neural data. v2 supplies actual neural-recording validation and probes larger inputs, alternative latents, downstream prediction, and limited-data behavior, substantially strengthening and qualifying those recommendations. Appendix corrections also repair concrete mathematical errors. Several new experiments remain briefly documented, limiting reproducibility, but the broader validation and explicit failure conditions provide a substantial net quality gain.
